en.title: KOTOR Remake 'Hopefully' Arriving in 2028, Says New Saber Exec
en.summary: A new executive at Saber Interactive has offered a potential release window for the long-awaited Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic remake. The game, announced in 2021, has faced a turbulent development cycle.
en.body:
The **Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic remake** has been shrouded in uncertainty since its announcement, but a recent statement from a new Saber Interactive executive has offered a potential, albeit tentative, release window. Steve Allison, who recently joined Saber as Chief Business Officer, mentioned in a public post that the studio is "preparing to do more self publishing and I'm here to organize the group in preparation of the lineup for 2028." He explicitly listed the **KOTOR remake** among these anticipated titles, adding, "hopefully [the] KOTOR remake and a few unannounced titles."

This mention comes after a period of significant upheaval for the project. Originally revealed in 2021 with Aspyr Media at the helm, development was later transferred to Saber Interactive in 2022. Since then, updates have been scarce, leading many fans to worry about the remake's status. While Saber Interactive has previously assured the game is "alive and well," specific timelines have remained elusive. Allison's statement, confirmed as genuine by a Saber representative, is the most concrete indication of a target year yet, even if it's couched in hopeful language.

## A Troubled Path to the Old Republic
The **KOTOR remake** has been a passion project for many, aiming to bring one of the most beloved RPGs of all time to modern hardware. The original **Knights of the Old Republic**, released in 2003, set a benchmark for narrative-driven RPGs with its deep lore, memorable characters, and impactful choices within the **Star Wars** universe. The journey of its remake, however, has been anything but smooth, marked by reported delays, studio changes, and the broader industry shifts impacting companies like Embracer Group, which owns Saber Interactive.

> "We are preparing to do more self publishing and I'm here to organize the group in preparation of the lineup for 2028 ... that includes Space Marine, [John] Wick, hopefully [the] KOTOR remake and a few unannounced titles." — Steve Allison

## Fan Hopes and Lingering Doubts
For the dedicated fanbase, any news about the **KOTOR remake** is significant. The game holds a special place in the hearts of **Star Wars** and RPG enthusiasts, and the prospect of experiencing **Revan's** story with updated graphics and gameplay mechanics is incredibly exciting. However, the "hopefully" in Allison's statement, coupled with the 2028 target, means fans will likely need to temper their expectations. The development of remakes and ambitious titles is complex, and delays are common, especially for projects with such a high level of anticipation and a storied development history.

## What's Next
While 2028 is the earliest potential release window mentioned, Saber Interactive has not provided an official release date. Fans will be eagerly awaiting further updates, particularly regarding gameplay reveals and more concrete development milestones, as the studio gears up for its proposed 2028 lineup.

content_raw: We got our yearly 'KOTOR remake is still alive' assurance back in March, but they must be making some real progress over there at Saber Interactive because here's a fresh one: Newly-minted chief business officer Steve Allison said in a recent post that "hopefully" the long-overdue remake will be out in, uhh, 2028. The statement was initially shared, as far as I can tell, on the Space Marine subreddit , and was made in response to an inquiry about Saber's intentions for monetization in Space Marine 2 and future games in the series. After denying that he'd been hired to "squeeze money" out of future Saber releases, Allison wrote, "We are preparing to do more self publishing and I'm here to organize the group in preparation of the lineup for 2028 ... that includes Space Marine, [John] Wick, hopefully [the] KOTOR remake and a few unannounced titles." A Saber Interactive rep confirmed with PC Gamer that it is indeed a genuine message from Allison, who is "incredibly excited" for the company's upcoming slate of games—although the rep added that it is not an official statement on the state or release targets of any of them. (Image credit: Steve Allison) The bulk of Allison's missive is dedicated to Saber's business model: Going hard on microtransactions is "not how we do our products," he wrote, adding that while the company may offer paid DLC for some games, it "can't repeat the voice pack DLC issue on SM2," a reference to Space Marine 2 DLC released earlier this year that went over very poorly with players . But it's the reference to KOTOR that caught my eye, along with many others . The Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic remake was announced in 2021 , and it hasn't exactly been smooth sailing since: Delays , denials , a studio swap , the whole Embracer implosion thing that saw Saber spun out as an independent business , and probably other hitches I've forgotten about have all contributed to an aura of mystery and confusion around the whole thing. The most recent pronouncement came in March, when Saber CEO Tim Willits said " it is still in development ." And nothing else. Allison's name-drop really isn't much more than that, except that it comes with a release target: An extremely hypothetical and vaguely defined release target, yes, but at this point we take what we can get. Coming at it from the other side, though, "hopefully 2028" while we're still just at the midpoint of 2026 pretty strongly suggests that there's still a lot of work to be done on the remake, and that means the potential for even more delays in the future.
